newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on flagging sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on flagging sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down slightly in dull trade, with most investors having little interest in trading on worsening market sentiment, dampened by rumours of further crackdown measures, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.249 points or 0.30 percent to 82.138 points on shrinking volume of 11.733 million shares worth $7.914 million.
According to one of the rumours, the government is planning to punish around 23 brokerages for contributing to volatile trading during market surges earlier this year, brokers said.
"The rumours about further clampdown measures are still in the market, which greatly depressed market sentiment," one broker said.
Another broker said overseas investors who were seen buying on the market during the surges early this year were now back on the sidelines.
"Domestic investors dominated the market with some institutions seen off-setting their positions while others took a wait-and-see attitude, resulting in today's dull trade," he said.
"Technical charts have shown signs that the market will move down further in the short term, but the index will see support between 75-78 points," a third broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 38 traded, with 17 down, nine flat and 12 up.
China First Pencil was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling, slipping $0.032 or 6.80 percent to $0.438 on volume of 447,700 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the most actively traded on profit-taking, down $0.012 or 1.40 percent to $0.844 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the second most actively traded on institutional support buying, gaining $0.006 or 0.44 percent to $1.362 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index fell on the same factors, but it was off an intraday low of 1,266.792 points thanks to institutional support buying in selective stocks, brokers said.
The index ended down 2.806 points or 0.21 percent to 1,307.821 points on volume of 546.201 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan.
But the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on support buying, ending up 26.410 points or 0.68 percent to 3,908.338 points.
Petroleum Long Champ was the biggest loser, plunging 1.07 yuan or 9.97 percent to 9.66 yuan on volume of 578,000 shares.
